newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope John Paul calls for tolerance towards gypsies.
newsitem.headline: Pope John Paul calls for tolerance towards gypsies.

text.p: Pope John Paul called on Monday for tolerance towards gypsies, one day after he put the first member of the nomadic people on the road to sainthood.

The Pope told thousands of gypsies at Sunday's beatification ceremony of Ceferino Jimenez Malla, an illiterate gypsy horse trader known as "El Pele", that recognition from the Roman Catholic church was a step towards ending intolerance.

"It is necessary to overcome ancient prejudices that lead you to suffer forms of discrimination and at times undesirable marginalisation of the gypsy population," the Pontiff told gypsies during an audience on Monday.
"El Pele in his path towards sainthood must be for you an example and an incentive for the full integration of your culture in the social environment around you," he added.
Some 40,000 people attended Sunday's ceremony in which the 76-year-old Pontiff beatified Jimenez, a Spanish gypsy who was shot during the 1936-39 civil war.

Jimenez, a deeply religious man who tried to improve relations between gypsies and non-gypsies, was arrested by an anti-clerical militia in 1936 after publicly defending a priest, and was later killed by a firing squad.
Beatification is the penultimate step before sainthood and is bestowed on people who showed heroic virtue in their lives.
Meanwhile, more than 1,000 gypsies met in the north Italian city of Verona on Monday to decide who should be the new "king" of the up to 10 million nomadic people living in Europe today.
Gypsies, who first came from India more than a thousand years ago, number around 110,000 in Italy. The Nazis killed about a half million gypsies in World War Two.
